description: DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS_BRIGHT, r<19.5) clustering sample, randomly down-sampled, as 3D points in comoving space: the main cosmic-web reveal.

fields.name: zMpc
fields.description: comoving z: towards Dec=+90 (ICRS north pole)

fields.name: redshift
fields.description: CMB-frame redshift z_cmb used for the distance (input Z is solar-system-barycentric)

fields.name: colorOrMag
fields.description: g-r colour, observed frame, from Galactic-extinction-corrected Legacy Surveys DR9 fluxes: -2.5*log10(flux_g_dered/flux_r_dered). Typical range ~0.2 (blue, star-forming) to ~1.8 (red, passive, higher z).

nullHandling: No nulls/NaN. 0 catalogue rows with non-positive g or r flux (colour undefined) were excluded from the sampling pool before down-sampling.
order: Uniform random sample drawn with a seeded partial Fisher-Yates shuffle (mulberry32 seed 20250210); records are in random order, so any prefix of N records is itself a uniform random subsample (use for progressive loading / level of detail).

coordinateFrame.axes: ICRS (J2000) equatorial Cartesian; x=(cos dec cos ra), y=(cos dec sin ra), z=(sin dec) times comoving distance
coordinateFrame.origin: observer (solar-system barycentre); the Milky Way is at the origin
coordinateFrame.positionsAre: redshift-space (derived): peculiar velocities not removed (Fingers of God in clusters, Kaiser flattening).

redshiftFrame.inputFrame: solar-system barycentric (DESI Redrock Z, as stored in the LSS catalogues)
redshiftFrame.conversion: 1+z_cmb = (1+z_bary) * gamma * (1 + beta*cos(theta)); beta = v/c, theta = angle to CMB dipole apex

cmbDipole.ref: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A1 (Planck 2018 results I), Sect. 5.3

cosmology.name: flat LambdaCDM, Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO (H0=67.66 km/s/Mpc, Omega_m=0.3111, Omega_Lambda=1-Omega_m, radiation neglected)
cosmology.ref: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6, Table 2 (last column)
cosmology.integration: D_C(z) = (c/H0) * int_0^z dz/sqrt(Om(1+z)^3 + OL); cumulative composite Simpson on a uniform grid dz=1e-5, linear interpolation (error < 1e-6 Mpc)

source.release: DESI DR1 (iron) LSS catalogs v1.5 - clustering .dat files
source.dataReleasePaper: DESI Collaboration et al. 2026, AJ 171, 285: "Data Release 1 of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument"
catalogPapers: Ross A.J. et al. 2025, JCAP 01, 125 (construction of DESI LSS catalogs)
DESI Collaboration 2025, JCAP 07, 017 (DESI 2024 II: sample definitions, characteristics and two-point clustering statistics)
source.license: CC BY 4.0 (DESI Data License); changes: columns subset, frame change, distance computation, random down-sampling

sampling.weightsIgnored: Clustering weights (WEIGHT, WEIGHT_FKP, completeness) are NOT applied: points are galaxies, not a density estimator.

selection.targetSelection: BGS BRIGHT: r < 19.5 (Legacy Surveys DR9), flux-limited -> number density falls steeply with redshift

footprint.summary: Partial sky: two caps. The NGC footprint spans roughly RA 110-270 deg (Dec ~ -10 to +80); the SGC footprint wraps through RA 0 (roughly RA 300-360 and 0-50 deg, Dec ~ -20 to +35). Rendered in 3D the survey appears as two thick wedge-shaped cones with the observer at the apex; empty directions are unobserved sky (DR1 = first year of DESI), not voids.
footprint.areaMethod: sum of occupied 0.5x0.5-deg RA/Dec cells (overestimates edges slightly)

grid.encoding: base64 bitmask, LSB-first within each byte; bit index k = raCell + 180*decCell; raCell = floor(RA/2deg) (0..179), decCell = floor((Dec+90)/2deg) (0..89); bit=1 means at least one galaxy in the cell

caveats: Wedges: DR1 covers only part of the sky; edges of the cones are survey boundaries.
Flux limit (BGS r<19.5): point density thins strongly beyond z~0.3; this is selection, not a real decline.
Redshift-space distortions: clusters stretched radially (Fingers of God), large-scale walls flattened (Kaiser effect).
Fibre-assignment incompleteness in DR1 is patchy (tile overlap pattern); weights that correct it are not applied.
